reviews.title: One of the worst social networks ever created!
reviews.pros: Nothing and nothing! At the beginning it seemed interesting to me, perhaps a place where I could write freely without any problems, at the beginning I trusted the social network, a new platform where I could insert my works, but not only were my works not seen by anyone, but In my opinion the site didn't even try to help me for a moment with the algorithm!
reviews.cons: Not only do you have an embarrassing character limit, but as soon as they see that you make a few more posts a day you are branded as a spammer and without thinking twice they block you and close your page as if you were a thief or a murderer!
reviews.overall: I have a blog that regularly writes reviews on books, films and video games, I posted my posts day after day and after a few months of hard work a guy reported me publicly as a spammer and Mastodon deleted my page without thinking twice! I tried to contact them but no one deigned to answer me after several weeks! I would say it is one of the worst social networks together with Tumblr, since they are very similar as art eliminators!

reviews.title: Bitterly disappointed
reviews.pros:
Easy to use, with practice. Easy to find other interested in the same things, (by use of hashtags etc).

Easy to upload links, and images.

Easy to follow others that on is interested in.

Easy to complain, block - e.g adult messages.
reviews.cons: Mastodon has cancelled my account. This time they cancelled me for "Inciting to Violence". This was simply not true.
reviews.overall:
I was expelled from Mastodon for supposedly "Inciting to violence".

The offending post was  a plea to restore funding to The United Nations Relief and Works Agency for Palestine Refugees in the Near East (UNRWA). The offending article did say that the arguments used by Israel were worthy of Goebbels.  Either Mastodon's monitors did not understand, or they were pushed by the Israel lobby to exclude me. I wrote no incentive to violence. Just incentive to humanitarian aid. I did put in an appeal merely saying that my post incentivised to aid, not violence. But my appeal was rejected.

reviews.title: Decent
reviews.pros: Decent. Open. It is what you make of it. Decent people. The conversations are very interesting and there's a wide range of topics to follow.
reviews.cons: Bit preachy. Ignore that. The UI is a bit heavy but very functional.
reviews.overall: Decent experience. Hell of a lot better than Twitter. I recommend it but you really have to go looking for the things you want to follow.

reviews.title: The way social is meant to be
reviews.pros: No cockamamie algorithms, quality content and discussion. Very few trolls, and easy to get them banned. Decent web interface. Mobile app Megalodon is great.
reviews.cons: Somewhat hard to duplicate original twitter follows, but in the end that doesn't matter.
reviews.overall: Excellent social network that fulfills my needs for news, insight, discussion of science, politics, and culture. No nazis and any trolls are short-lived. Free, no ads, and I pay (willingly) $1/month to my instance and $1/month to Gargron. Worth it.

reviews.title: Horror
reviews.cons: Its a clubhouse for the woke community, disgusting people.
reviews.overall: Removed my account as fast as I could.

reviews.title: Mastodon following same road as Twitter. :(
reviews.pros: At first it seemed to be cool and laidback - the exact opposite of how Twitter under the MuskRAT is now being run.
reviews.cons: Really sad that a site that showed such promise is now starting down the same road as Twitter, banning people on false accusations of rule/policy violations based on the whims of mods/admins who are letting the power go to their heads. They are in effect practicing the same double-standards as most other social media, allowing certain groups to do and say whatever they want, while penalizing others.
reviews.overall: Not good. Wound up being banned for rule violations I did not commit due to pressure from a special interest group who I opposed for bullying and libeling others. I WOULD NOT recommend this platform.

reviews.title: Mastodon is Better Than Alternatives
reviews.pros:
Open Source.

NOT Centralized.

NOT owned by a single company.

Thousands of Distributed Mastodon Servers.

Can edit posts.

NO ALGORITHMS!

Users have much more control.

Moderation.

Less Drama.

Positivity.
reviews.cons:
Not as many famous people on Mastodon compared to Twitter

Some new users have a hard time finding the right Mastodon server. I recommend looking and medium and smaller Mastodon instances
reviews.overall: Mastodon is popular for a reason. It supports many of the same features as Twitter. Open source and actively developed.. A Ruby on Rails, PostgreSQL, Redis app!

reviews.title: Good If You Don't Value Your Patience
reviews.pros:
A decentralized network is a great premise. People are free to make and run their own servers how they wish, and connect with other servers how they wish.

Overall, people are a tad nicer here, as I have seen firsthand.

Also, it's impossible to be truly banned, as being banned from one server doesn't restrict you from joining any other server.
reviews.cons: The place's premise is also its downfall in a sense. The "moderators" and "administrators" that run these servers aren't hired professionals, they're just some guy. In turn, they tend to not be the best at their job if you pick the wrong server. My account was terminated once for a single strike, and I will gladly never use that server again.
reviews.overall: Overall, it's twitter for tech nerds and people who don't like who's running twitter. Once the hurdles of "what is an instance" and "who do i follow" are over, it's a pretty decent place.

reviews.title: Banned
reviews.pros: I was on there for about two weeks. I received a warning over a picture that showed a camel toe and permanently banned for saying little white dove. I think I'll just stay on TikTok. They allow people who have views different from their own,
reviews.cons:
No logical appeal process. 

Banned for no reason.
reviews.overall: Lousy, they already banned me without a reason and run a worse site than I have seen so far in.

reviews.title: It's decent
reviews.pros: Has some cool features. The decentralized nature of it is cool, although there are drawbacks to it. So far it's been a decent experience.
reviews.cons: It's much harder for the average person to use compared to Twitter. Also, moderation seems to differ between servers. Some moderators on some servers will ban you if they do not like you, or disagree with your ideology. Apparently moderators can also see your direct messages.
reviews.overall: Overall it's a decent alternative to Twitter, but I am going to stick with Twitter mainly. Mastodon still has a lot of room to grow but it's not there yet.

reviews.title: This site must be banned as it goes against public safety
reviews.pros: Nothing at all. It's overly complicated, juvenile, unusable, poor programming besides the racism and violence.
reviews.overall: It has been traumatic and painful being on Mastodon and hell every day. Not only did I feel unsafe, others were complaining as well. Received threats when protesting against these hellish posts. This site is mafia land.
